clue.text: Meat for all at freeway junction

parts.note: something for all is universal, common to everyone
a joint is a large cut of meat for roasting

explanation.surface: A roadside caterer serves a roast for everyone at a motorway interchange.
explanation.walkthrough: The road picture is a blind: the junction is a mechanical coupling that lets two shafts move freely at an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: This coupling joins two rotating shafts while allowing free movement in any direction, a free-moving junction.

clue.text: She may have an uncle in the South of France I hear

indicators.note: the speaker reports what reaches the ear, so the word is said aloud and respelt

parts.note: Nice is the best-known city of the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A woman with a relative living down on the Riviera, or so the gossip goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is someone with an uncle by definition.

clue.text: Put change in it if you want to save

definitions.text: Put change in it if you want to save

indicators.note: to change the word save is to rearrange its four letters

explanation.surface: Advice to drop your loose coins into a pot if you hope to put money by.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a money jar for loose change; in the wordplay 'change' is the signal to rearrange 'save'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental pot is a container you might drop coins into for safekeeping.

clue.text: Order to revise categories of tourist-centre

definitions.meaning: to sort again is to rearrange into categories a second time
a holiday town where visitors flock

explanation.surface: An instruction to reorganise the kinds of holiday destination on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as RE-SORT, the word is an instruction to sort again.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorting again means regrouping into classes, and a seaside holiday town is the other sense.

clue.text: Modified line in unusual sand worms

indicators.note: one rearranged word is placed within the other, as line sits inside sand
sand in an unusual form has its letters rearranged
line once modified has its letters put in a new order

explanation.surface: A drawing of worms in odd sand with an altered line through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worms' looks like a verb but is the definition; 'unusual' and 'Modified' each rearrange their own word, one placed within the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Segmented worms such as earthworms and leeches form this zoological group.

clue.text: Cheat society ? Not these flat-managers of course

parts.note: to jockey can mean to trick or manoeuvre someone unfairly
a club is an association or society

explanation.surface: Is this a fraudulent gang? No, merely the people running the racetrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' is flat racing (no jumps) and 'course' a racecourse: the body governing British horse racing, not landlords.
explanation.definitionFit: This body long governed British horse racing, including flat races run on courses.

clue.text: It provides an artificial hatchway

parts.note: hatchway reads as a means of hatching eggs, not a ship's opening, and an artificial one is a heated machine

explanation.surface: A ship's fitting that gives a false trapdoor.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated cabinet keeps eggs warm so chicks hatch without the hen.

clue.text: Fictitious title to isolated hoarding-site

definitions.meaning: the name of Stevenson's pirate novel, a work of fiction
a lonely piece of land surrounded by sea where riches are hidden

explanation.surface: A made-up name given to a remote spot where valuables are stashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's novel title and, read literally, a sea-girt place holding buried riches.

clue.text: Where Cockneys don't aspire to go on Bank Holiday ?

definitions.text: Where Cockneys don't aspire to go on Bank Holiday ?

parts.words: Where Cockneys don't aspire to go on Bank Holiday ?
parts.note: aspire hints at aspirate: Cockneys drop their aitches, so the London park they flock to loses both its initial H sounds

explanation.surface: A place working-class Londoners have no ambition to visit on their day off.
explanation.walkthrough: In fact Cockneys did go there on Bank Holidays; what they don't do is aspirate, saying 'Ampstead 'Eath. A Bank Holiday is a British public holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: This north London open space hosted famous Bank Holiday fairs beloved of East Enders.

clue.text: Five insane disorders for Herb Bennet

indicators.note: disorders works as a verb here, jumbling the letters of the pieces before it

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
the setter splits this word as 'in sane': the word sane, with V put in it before the jumble

explanation.surface: Five mad derangements recorded for a man called Herb.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'insane', which the setter means as 'in sane': V goes in SANE and the whole is jumbled. Herb Bennet is the plant's old name.
explanation.definitionFit: Herb bennet, or wood avens, is a common hedgerow plant of the rose family.

clue.text: Musical series made for two?

parts.note: the old song about a bicycle made for two suggests a cycle that is also a sequence of songs

explanation.surface: A run of tunes written as a duet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy Bell' sings of 'a bicycle made for two', so a cycle made for two is also a set of songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of linked art songs performed in sequence forms one musical work.

clue.text: Lord, look at him !

definitions.meaning: a member of the nobility sitting in the upper house
to look closely or squint at someone

explanation.surface: An exclamation drawing attention to a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A titled noble is one sense; gazing intently is the other.

clue.text: Its high-wire performance moved the public

definitions.text: Its high-wire performance moved the public

parts.words: Its high-wire performance moved the public
parts.note: high-wire suggests a circus act that stirs an audience, but here it is overhead electric cables powering a vehicle carrying passengers

explanation.surface: A tightrope walker's act brought the crowd to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: This electric bus draws power from overhead cables while carrying passengers along streets.

clue.text: Stubborn as Angelico in the parsonage

indicators.note: the painter's title is placed within the clergyman's house

parts.note: a rectory is the house of a parish priest
the painter Fra Angelico, whose title Fra means brother

explanation.surface: As obstinate as a famous friar-painter lodging at the vicarage.
explanation.walkthrough: Fra Angelico was an Italian Renaissance friar and painter; only his title is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate and resisting control, as an unmanageable person or a resistant illness is.

clue.text: Meddle with the packer

definitions.meaning: a tool or person that tamps, pressing material down firmly

explanation.surface: Interfering with someone who packs boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Interfering is one sense; a tool that rams down tobacco or earth is the other.

clue.text: Playwright of Teesdale

definitions.meaning: the market town in Teesdale, County Durham

explanation.surface: A dramatist from a valley in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Middleton wrote Jacobean tragedies; a Durham dale town shares the surname.

clue.text: He may be a master of form

definitions.text: He may be a master of form

parts.words: He may be a master of form
parts.note: master suggests an expert in style, but a schoolmaster takes a form, a school class

explanation.surface: An artist who has perfected style.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolteacher, or master, takes a form, the British word for a school class.

clue.text: Hence a quiet bit to eat in the bathroom

parts.note: so means therefore, hence
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a dish is a prepared serving of food

explanation.surface: Therefore one has a quiet snack while in the bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tray beside the bath or basin holds a cake of washing bar.

clue.text: My Jo's shelter

definitions.meaning: Burns's song 'John ..., my jo' addresses an old husband as dear
the corrugated-steel garden air-raid refuge of the Second World War

explanation.surface: My sweetheart's refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Burns's poem names the husband addressed as 'my jo'; the wartime backyard air-raid refuge bore the same surname.

clue.text: Painter from Ward!

parts.note: ward means guard, and with a letter I added the guard becomes a Venetian painter

explanation.surface: An artist who came out of a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Francesco Guardi painted Venetian views; his name splits as GUARD (ward) plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Francesco Guardi was an eighteenth-century Venetian view painter.

clue.text: Of this, an alternative

parts.note: the phrase of this has a single formal word that may stand in its place

explanation.surface: A choice offered regarding the matter in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal or formal adverb meaning concerning this document or matter.

clue.text: Hovercraft for the police, right? Maybe

indicators.note: maybe indicates the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A question whether an air-cushion vessel is right for the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hovercraft' suggests the air-cushion boat, but it means any craft that hovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor aircraft can hang stationary in the air, so it is literally a craft that hovers.

clue.text: Defile the earth

definitions.meaning: the ground in which plants grow

explanation.surface: Polluting the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: To dirty something is one sense; the ground plants grow in is the other.

clue.text: The way of revolution for the satellites

definitions.text: The way of revolution for the satellites

parts.words: The way of revolution for the satellites
parts.note: revolution suggests political uprising in satellite states, but it is the circling path of moons

explanation.surface: The road to uprising for Soviet client states.
explanation.definitionFit: A moon or spacecraft follows a curved path round a planet as it revolves.

clue.text: Misses German being spoken

parts.note: misses spoken is missus, a wife, and a German wife or Mrs has a German title

explanation.surface: Someone who regrets not hearing German.
explanation.definitionFit: The German title for a married woman corresponds to Mrs.

clue.text: I.e., tour has sanction

annotationWithheld.why: I.e., tour has sanction (9): AUTHORISE is an anagram of I.E. + TOUR + HAS, but no clue word signals the anagram; every word is fodder except the definition, so the op has no indicator

clue.text: A good fellow, but Communist at heart ?

definitions.meaning: ... Goodfellow is another name for Puck, the mischievous sprite
the bird is red at the breast, and red means communist

explanation.surface: A decent chap, though secretly a leftist.
explanation.definitionFit: Puck's alternative name and a bird with a red breast.

clue.text: The king in Shakespeare played two parts

definitions.text: The king in Shakespeare played two parts

parts.words: The king in Shakespeare played two parts
parts.note: played two parts suggests an actor doubling roles, but this history play itself comes in Part One and Part Two

explanation.surface: An actor doubled as a monarch in a Shakespeare production.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's history of the fourth Lancastrian monarch is written as Part 1 and Part 2.
